gen_risks.description: Integration and operation of first-of-a-kind (FOAK) carbon capture technology at an operational cement plant may encounter unforeseen technical failure or underperformance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform independent technical assurance through WSP and ensure adherence to standardized CCS Network Code operational specifications.
gen_risks.evidence: first at-scale UK cement plant incorporating Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology

gen_risks.description: Alignment delays with spurline infrastructure construction could delay project Final Investment Decision and push back Commercial Operation Date by up to 5 months.
gen_risks.mitigation: Synchronize development timelines across capture and spurline teams and establish Cluster Sponsor Function oversight of cluster construction schedules.
gen_risks.evidence: align with their spurline timelines, resulting in a subsequent 5-month delay to COD

gen_risks.description: Cross-chain operational dependencies between the Padeswood capture plant and the Liverpool Bay transport and storage network create delivery and integration risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish Cluster Sponsor Function oversight to manage government-owned cross-chain delivery and operating model integration risks.
gen_risks.evidence: Managing government-owned cross-chain delivery risks and operating model integration risks.

gen_risks.description: Failure to meet performance thresholds for CO2 capture volume could trigger contractual under-delivery penalties and reduce ongoing revenue support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate performance thresholds and under-delivery safeguards into the ICC Contract with active performance monitoring by the Low Carbon Contracts Company.
gen_risks.evidence: performance thresholds, safeguards against under-delivery, and contractual clauses covering change in law

gen_risks.description: Financial risk under the Revenue Support Agreement from higher operational costs or unexpected lower carbon capture volumes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure revenue support under the Industrial Carbon Capture Contract with payments tied directly to performance and captured CO2 volumes.

gen_risks.description: Discontinuation of the Padeswood project pre- or post-FID leading to loss of capital investment and failure to demonstrate cement sector CCUS.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement Government Support Package provisions, enforce clear conditions precedent, and maintain oversight through the Cluster Sponsor Function.

gen_risks.description: Exchequer funding liabilities arising from Secretary of State Direct Agreements exceeding initially allocated support thresholds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Cap overall support within the £21.7bn Final Funding Envelope and subject agreements to strict central government financial governance.
gen_risks.evidence: 5.4.3 Exchequer funding Secretary of State direct agreements (SoSDA)

gen_risks.description: Risk of fraud or misuse of public spending through capital grants or ongoing operational business model support payments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Administer grant payments through DESNZ Central Grants & Loans team using Open Book Model financial reporting and ongoing compliance auditing.

gen_risks.description: Financial sensitivity to energy price volatility, macroeconomic inflation, and capital cost overruns impacting project economic viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy joint Open Book Models updated with DESNZ cost assessment templates and perform independent financial assurance through EY.

gen_risks.description: Cross-cutting and cross-chain financial and operational risks across the HyNet cluster impacting Padeswood's economics.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactively manage cluster-wide risks via the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function and align contractual terms across connected network users.

gen_risks.description: Unabated cement operations subject to rising carbon prices leading companies to shift production overseas (carbon leakage).
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy CCUS at Padeswood using CIF capital grants and ICC Contract revenue support to sustain domestic cement sector competitiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Without investment in CCUS, companies may de-prioritise their UK interests and shift production elsewhere

gen_risks.description: Governance fragmentation across multiple regulatory and administrative bodies (Ofgem, LCCC, DESNZ CGL, Cluster Sponsor Function) causing decision bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Post-FID Operating Model with clear functional division between LCCC, DESNZ CGL, Ofgem, and central coordination by the Cluster Sponsor Function.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood will be overseen through a range of bodies including: Ofgem... LCCC... DESNZ CGL... DESNZ Cluster Function Team

gen_risks.description: Introduction of the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism in 2027 placing unabated UK cement sites at a competitive disadvantage against international producers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate CCUS deployment at Padeswood to establish low-carbon cement production capability ahead of 2027 CBAM implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: The UK Carbon-Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)... will be introduced in 2027. However, unabated UK sites would be competing with sites overseas.

gt_risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) risk. RSA would be paid to the T&S Company (Eni) in two circumstances: where the network is underutilised, and where users are unavailable to inject CO2 and therefore are not paying user fees. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.1, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Padeswood joining the T&S network will reduce the level of network underutilisation and will therefore reduce RSA payments to the T&SCo.

gt_risks.description: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood: the potential for Padeswood to be unable to continue under the business model contract due to the actions of another party or events outside its control - a large-scale, programme-wide issue (e.g. leakage), a prolonged T&S issue, or external events such as Qualifying Change in Law (QCiL), Qualifying Shutdown Events, or Force Majeure. Projects connected via a spurline can also be exposed to an additional risk if the spurline FID is taken after T&S FID, which is not within the capture project's control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.2, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The risk of having to make a discontinuation payment to Padeswood is judged to be a remote contingent liability given that it is very unlikely (<1%); spurline-timing risk is treated as a variation of the existing cross-chain risks already protected by the business model.

gt_risks.description: Exchequer funding / Secretary of State direct agreement (SoSDA) risk: LCCC is only liable to make payments to the extent it has received sufficient funds from HMG, creating a risk that Padeswood would have no recourse under its private-law contract with LCCC to obtain payments owed if HMG funding to LCCC were insufficient. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.3, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The Secretary of State will sign a direct agreement with Padeswood (to which LCCC is also party) to fund payments directly where LCCC fails to pay; this does not increase DESNZ's overall liabilities or create a contingent liability, as it is an intragroup transaction.

gt_risks.description: Fraud risk across the CCUS programme's grant and contract payments. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.4, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: A CCUS Fraud Management Strategy is being developed specifying the programme's strategic approach to deterrence, prevention, detection, and management of fraud and error, including counter-fraud governance and reporting structures and high-quality fraud risk assessments (FRAs) for the different tranches of the CCUS programme.

gt_risks.description: Financial sensitivities: several contractual terms are 'locked in' at Padeswood FID, but drivers of the financial impact continue to move post-FID - notably the carbon market price (Low ETS series used as the reference price for the extension period) and the opex reopener (higher opex expenditure payments), both of which could result in higher subsidy. Other financial sensitivities have the effect of reducing total subsidy. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.5, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to estimate the scale of potential subsidy increase from each driver; offsetting sensitivities are also identified and tracked.

gt_risks.description: Cross-chain and cross-cutting risks. Cross-chain risks are risks the private sector is exposed to through the network but cannot mitigate against - T&S Construction delay, Padeswood Construction Delay, Padeswood Underperformance, T&S Underperformance, and Discontinuation Provisions; Padeswood joining the HyNet cluster increases HMG's exposure to compensation payments should the T&S network fail or become unavailable. Cross-cutting risks - inflation risk, carbon price risk, and OpEx risk - are those which are challenging for the private sector to price or relate to events outside their control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.6, p.14-15; overlaps in subject matter with the Economic Case's Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal tables, p.10-11, which quantify the value-for-money impact of the same named risks but are a modelling input rather than a risk-register entry, and are excised from planning text for leakage safety but not scored here.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Risk allocation is designed so that each risk sits with the party best placed to manage it; the business model contracts and Network Code are structured to limit and price cross-chain exposure.
